info.label: Blue Note
info.desc: Come Away with Me is the debut album of pianist and singer Norah Jones, released February 26, 2002 on Blue Note Records. Although genre classification has been disputed, Jones' mellow style and playing on Come Away with Me is recognized as contemporary jazz. The album's critical and commercial success was a breakthrough for Jones in 2002, as it reached the top of the Billboard 200 chart and several jazz charts. The album also topped many critics' "albums of the year" lists and gathered major music awards in the process, including eight Grammy Awards. Following initial sales, Come Away with Me .

podcast.body: Norah Jones initially found the 6 PM daily departure rule imposed by producer Arif Mardin during its recording to be "ridiculous" as she was used to recording late, but it ultimately worked out well. The album's massive success led to her photo on the New York Post next to Saddam Hussein's and details about her apartment's rent in the daily news, making it impossible for her to go home due to the intense scrutiny. She describes the fame from this record as "bananas" and doesn't wish to experience that level of overwhelming attention again. "I don't think I would want it to be like my first record ever again. That was just too much."

podcast.body: Released on Blue Note Records, this was Nora Jones' "juggernaut debut album" that came out in February 2002. Before its official release, actress Sandra Bullock had an advanced copy and sought to include music from it in her movie "Two Weeks Notice." The album's rise to popularity was described as a "slow study rise." Nora wrote only two or three songs on the album, with the rest contributed by Jesse Harris, Lee Alexander, and various covers. The initial recording session for the album with producer Craig Street involved recording 21 songs in a week and mixing them immediately, but the album was rejected due to perceived issues with the mixes. Ultimately, three "amazing takes" from this session were used on the final record. "Nora released her Juggernaut debut album Come Away With Me on Blue Note Records way back in 2002."

podcast.body: This album, by jazz-pop vocalist Nora Jones, won Album of the Year in 2003. It was cited as an example of a "Starbucks album" – easy listening, jazzy, or rustic-sounding CDs often sold near coffee chain counters, which received an early boost from such placements. "2003 winner Come Away With Me by Jazz Pop Vocalist Nora Jones."
